abstract: A tape-to-film process was used by the California Speech and Hearing Association (CSHA) to produce a 35-minute black-and-white sound film which consisted of six recorded 5-minute sessions with speech-handicapped children. The film was made at minimum cost. The use of two cameras gave added versatility and the ability to do retakes almost immediately eliminated the need for film editing while providing an accurate and acceptable finished print.
